## [**7. Medicaid Expansion Impact**]{style="color: teal;"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5

library(ggplot2)

medicaid_data <- data.frame(
  state_type = rep(c("Expanded", "Did Not Expand"), 3),
  outcome = rep(c("Uninsured (%)", "Mortality\n(per 100k)", 
                  "Financial hardship (%)"), each = 2),
  value = c(8, 16, 850, 920, 15, 25)
)

medicaid_data$outcome <- factor(medicaid_data$outcome,
                                levels = c("Uninsured (%)", 
                                          "Mortality\n(per 100k)",
                                          "Financial hardship (%)"))

ggplot(medicaid_data, aes(x = outcome, y = value, fill = state_type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 0)), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Expanded" = "#2E7D32",
                               "Did Not Expand" = "#C62828")) +
  labs(
    title = "Medicaid Expansion Impact (2014-2020)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Value",
    fill = NULL,
    caption = "Sources: Sommers et al. (2017), Miller & Wherry (2019)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", color = "#008080"),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )
```

## [**8. Gig Economy**]{style="color: teal;"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

gig_comparison <- data.frame(
  benefit = c("Health insurance", "Paid sick leave", "Retirement", 
              "Workers' comp", "Unemployment", "Predictable schedule"),
  traditional = c(85, 75, 65, 100, 100, 80),
  gig = c(15, 5, 10, 0, 0, 20)
)

gig_long <- gig_comparison %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(traditional, gig), 
               names_to = "type", 
               values_to = "pct")

gig_long$benefit <- factor(gig_long$benefit, 
                           levels = rev(c("Health insurance", "Paid sick leave", 
                                         "Retirement", "Workers' comp",
                                         "Unemployment", "Predictable schedule")))

ggplot(gig_long, aes(x = pct, y = benefit, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(pct, "%")), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("traditional" = "#2E7D32", "gig" = "#C62828"),
    labels = c("Gig/Contract", "Traditional")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Traditional vs. Gig Economy Benefits",
    x = "Percentage (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Pew Research Center (2021), BLS"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 110)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", color = "#008080"),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
  )
```

Precarious work = precarious health

# [**9. Community vs. Population Assessments**]{style="color: teal;"}

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## [**9. Two Approaches**]{style="color: teal;"}

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Community Assessment**

- Specific neighborhood
- Involves residents
- Assets + needs
- Action plan

**Example:** South Side Chicago food deserts
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Population Assessment**

- Larger area
- Administrative data
- Disease patterns
- Surveillance

**Example:** CDC state diabetes rates
:::
:::

Both answer different questions
